Hi Laura,

Thanks for the heads up last week. Acme's security team is moving through our SIG review and we need an up-to-date list of Redwood's subprocessors for the SIG (vendors that process customer data or receive telemetry). Specifically can you confirm:

- All cloud providers (primary/backup) and regions used for customer workloads and logs
- Observability/telemetry vendors (who receives metrics/traces and whether telemetry contains PII or request payloads)
- Support/case management tools and whether support engineers or vendors can access request/response bodies
- Any recent changes to the subprocessor roster in the last 6 months

If possible, please attach a spreadsheet or CSV with vendor name, purpose, data categories accessed, and links to any SOC2 or ISO evidence. Also flag any subprocessors that have access to plaintext customer content.

We aim to complete the SIG by end of next week — appreciate a reply by EOD today if you can.

Thanks,

Laura — attaching the draft inventory CSV and pasting a quick summary below. I pulled from the vendor registry and change log (last update 2026-05-27).

[Attachment: subprocessors_inventory_v1.csv]

Quick summary (vendor | purpose | data categories | access level | notes):
- AWS (us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 backup) | Cloud compute & storage | Encrypted at rest; customer data stored per customer region | Redwood infra engineers (no plaintext unless customer config) | SOC2 report on Drive link
- GCP (europe-west4 for EU customers) | Backup storage & analytics | Metadata + logs | limited infra access | used for region-specific backups
- TelemetryFlow Inc. | Observability (metrics/traces) | Aggregated metrics, traces; small subset of obfuscated request metadata; no full request bodies retained | telemetry team + TelemetryFlow support (redacted by default) | we push traces with PII redaction rule v3
- Intercom Inc. | Customer support (case mgmt) | Support notes, case metadata, redacted logs | support engineers; Intercom support only via API keys; no direct access to raw request bodies by default | access is ticket-scoped
- Zendesk (legacy customers) | Support | Case metadata only | limited | planning migration
- S3 Transfer Partner (vendor for on-prem transfer) | Data transfer / import | Customer-provided payloads during onboarding | transfer operators under NDA; access logged and time-limited | used for one-off onboarding flows
- KMS Provider (KeyMaster) | Key management | Key metadata; Redwood controls key material | Redwood crypto team only | HSM-backed

Notes: last 6 months changes — added TelemetryFlow (2026-04-01) and S3 Transfer Partner for a specific onboarding flow (2026-03-15). SOC2 is current (Type II 2026-03). I included links in the CSV.

Marcus

Thanks Marcus — two clarifications:
- TelemetryFlow receives traces/metrics but we apply the PII redaction pipeline (rule set v3) before export. We do not forward full customer request/response bodies to TelemetryFlow.
- Intercom cases include snippets of user-submitted text copied from support forms; support engineers can see those snippets in the case view, but we redact request bodies in the logs. Support partners are bound by our DPA and undergo quarterly access reviews.

I'll add a short note to the CSV about the redaction guarantees and include the access review cadence. Also: we should include the contact for TelemetryFlow SOC/assurance (they provided an ISO cert).

—Stephanie
